dedupe_keys.name: building types map of germany 10 m

description: This dataset maps the predominant building type in every 10 metre pixel of Germany where building density exceeds 25 per cent. It was produced by Franz Schug, David Frantz, Sebastian van der Linden and Patrick Hostert at Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin and the University of Greifswald, and is described in PLOS ONE (2021). A random forest classifier applied to Sentinel-1 radar time series of 2017 and Sentinel-2 optical time series of 2018 separates four classes: single-family residential buildings, multi-family residential buildings, commercial and industrial buildings, and lightweight structures. Coverage is the whole of Germany. Access: version 1.0 was published on Zenodo on 12 March 2021 as 30 by 30 kilometre tiles in one zip of about 120 MB. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0; free. Caveats: pixel-level predictions with classification error, only where buildings cover more than a quarter of the pixel, and a 2017-2018 snapshot. Simulation uses are building-type layers for exposure and vulnerability models, heat and energy demand mapping, and population disaggregation. Related records: GlobalBuildingAtlas and the EU building density map.
